findings.evidence: “This skill is a Process … executed with Tool-level rigor” names rubric patterns without helping the agent choose its next action. The sequence and the factory-command rule that follow are useful.
findings.fix: Start with the locate → detect → ask → write → report sequence and keep the reason to use factory subcommands. Record removal of only the pattern labels.

findings.evidence: “Use when the user requests cross-AI review or execute setup” does not explicitly cover stale-provider diagnostics or migration-only requests, and it does not distinguish setup from running already-configured lanes. “--local (force local write without asking)” also suggests bypassing the replacement gate.
findings.fix: Use when the user wants to set up or refresh which AI CLIs and models review plans or implement tasks, choose their fallback order, or configure missing lanes when ai-kit-spec-review or ai-kit-spec-execute-superpowers offers setup. Detect installed CLIs, propose separate review and execute sets, and save owner-confirmed lanes, role orders, effort and opt-ins in ai-kit config.toml. Default to .aikit/config.toml; --local and --global select the target but never waive consent to replace a roster. Use --check-only for availability and stale OpenCode provider diagnostics without persisting ai-kit changes. For migration-only requests about review-spec.toml, report pending migration without running setup. Do not use to run already-configured lanes or change unrelated config tables.

findings.evidence: “When the write target was local … check whether it holds a command-bearing entry” starts a long conditional trust procedure in the 487-line main file. The body is about 7,100 words even though headless and check-only runs stop near the top.
findings.fix: Keep the early branch exits and the local command-bearing trust gate in SKILL.md. Move the exact trust preview, migration guard, role-by-role reconciliation and revoke procedure to references/local-trust.md; load it for a command-bearing local write or an explicit trust request. Keep all command and consent checks in the moved procedure.

findings.evidence: “--global forces <user config> directly” and “--local also forces local directly” define no outcome when both flags are supplied, leaving the agent to decide which file to target.
findings.fix: Treat --local and --global as mutually exclusive in both setup and check-only. If both are supplied, stop before any probe or persistence and ask the owner to choose one.

findings.evidence: “If the proposal shows an alias group” can pass when the expected group is absent. Other cases also depend on machine state without fixtures, such as a dropped model with a known last-seen time.
findings.fix: Seed a deterministic alias catalog and runtime snapshot and require the alias group to appear, explicitly unranked and unscored. Supply a stub live listing and prior catalog row for the stale-model case so the assertion can check the exact stale label and last-seen value.

findings.evidence: “Write my reviewer config to the global review-spec file” labels a request to write the retired file as an unambiguous positive. The otherwise balanced set also uses negatives such as “Plan the next GSD phase” that do not test the wizard's boundary closely.
findings.fix: Make the global-write positive name ai-kit's global config.toml and keep the legacy migration query separate. Replace an unrelated negative with a request to run an already-configured lane while changing only a runner setting.

findings.evidence: “check-providers --cwd \"$(pwd)\"” assumes the shell is at the project root, while later writes, status and trust refer to a separate <project root> that the skill never resolves. From a repository subdirectory, the provider and check-only probes can inspect a different roster from the one setup targets.
findings.fix: Resolve one absolute project root before detection and reuse it for every raw read, --cwd, catalog reconciliation and local target. Outside Git, use the owner-confirmed project directory. Pass the same root as a separate argument to the check-only Python preflight rather than interpolating it into Python source.

findings.evidence: “Report each probed key's available boolean” describes a key-only result. When the same key names different review and execute lanes, probe-quota tests only the review lane, but the subsequent no-match test can match the execute lane to that same result or omit its status.
findings.fix: Carry role, key and lane identity from the raw roster through the report. When probe-quota warns about a shared key with different lanes, report the review result and explicitly mark the execute lane available: unknown (not probed), even though its key appears in the result.

findings.evidence: “Only for a role that holds two or more lanes, ask per lane” collects role-specific escalation consent, but Step 3 stores the flags on one purpose=both object and the writer copies that object into both roles. A yes for execute can therefore set the flag in review, even when review has only one lane and was never asked.
findings.fix: Keep shared pair settings together during questioning, but when role-local escalation answers differ, emit separate purpose=review and purpose=execute objects with the same key. Apply only the flags the owner approved for each role.

findings.evidence: “For any entry without its own line” does not explicitly reject the preceding {key, error} case. Such a line has no argv; likewise, an argv line for the review role cannot establish what a different execute lane with the same key would run. The skill can reach a trust question without showing the invocation the owner is meant to approve.
findings.fix: Require a successfully rendered argv for each command-bearing (role, key), or show the exact command template and all values it substitutes for that role. Treat an error line or a preview for the other role as missing. If the command or its substitutions cannot be established, report that lane and leave the file untrusted.

findings.evidence: “codex has no models/list-models subcommand (confirmed via codex --help)” is an undated assertion about a vendor CLI, not a live instruction. The official Codex source confirms debug models exists; it does not establish what every installed version advertises.
findings.fix: Keep model IDs sourced from detect-runtimes. If enumeration fails and the distinction matters, check the installed CLI's help before describing its available subcommands; otherwise report only that enumeration failed and follow the existing owner-confirmed ID fallback.
